sheets.name: 00 README
values: START HERE | Lunar Surface Complexity Model v0.6
Working AIAA Space & Missiles Group testbed — designed for review, critique, and population with real mission data

A working Lunar Surface implementation of the committee complexity framework. It combines mission taxonomy, peer-population control, relative-rank complexity scoring, provenance discipline, and a separate experimental resource/stress layer.
It is not a finished standard, validated predictive failure model, or replacement for the Bearden-derived complexity methodology.

Mission parameters are converted to relative ranks within an approved comparison population and combined into a normalized Complexity Index. Comparison population matters: global, domain, class, and peer-group results may differ.
The 28-parameter Lunar Surface set is a proposed working domain implementation across Structural, Functional, Technology, Environment, Performance, Logistics, and Programmatic families.
Resource Adequacy and Stress Ratio are deliberately separate from the core index. They are hypotheses to be calibrated against historical cost, schedule, rework, anomaly, and outcome data.

1) Define mission/system and peer group.  2) Populate sourced raw attributes.  3) Convert to relative ranks.  4) Calculate core CI.  5) Run resource/stress tests separately.  6) Compare with actual outcomes.

The '08 Model Tests' sheet contains synthetic low/moderate/high architectures for a sanity check. These are illustrative only; they test model directionality and monotonic behavior, not statistical validity.
Open '01 Dashboard' first for the operating picture. Use '06 Parameter Dictionary' to discuss what should be measured and '07 Pilot Cohort' to select the first real systems.
Do not overwrite sourced mission values with estimates without marking provenance/status. Keep taxonomy version, parameter-set version, dataset version, and model version traceable.
Meeting view: KPIs, complexity profile, stress table, Phase-I ask, lead package
Earlier operational-overlay prototype retained because the Stress Test references it. Use 05 Lunar Surface Model as the current Lunar Surface scoring engine.

sheets.name: 03 Volunteer Map
values: SSTC Complexity Initiative — Domain & Task Lead Map
Each volunteer role owns a defined model product so data collection, normalization, analysis, and publication remain compatible across domains.
Orbit/regime, comm, autonomy, propulsion, mission purpose
Lander, rover, power, ISRU, habitat, logistics

We are seeking volunteers to lead individual mission domains and support specific modeling tasks. Each role has a defined product: domain leads build and validate peer mission cohorts; parameter leads define complexity drivers; statistical leads develop normalization and uncertainty methods; database/data-quality leads make the model reproducible; and standards/publication leads carry results into AIAA products. Members can volunteer either as a domain lead or for a bounded technical task.

sheets.name: 06 Parameter Dictionary
values: Lunar Surface Complexity Parameter Dictionary — Working v0.3

Source-grounded attribute families with Lunar Surface operational parameters. Scores are relative ranks within an approved peer population; the parameter set is a proposed domain pilot, not a replacement for the Bearden core.
Count of independently deployed or operated surface/flight elements
Distinct hardware/software/operational interfaces crossing subsystem or organization boundaries
Degree to which subsystem performance depends on other systems or shared services
Critical deployments, emplacement, assembly or reconfiguration events after launch
Distinct operational modes requiring different control logic or sequencing
Functions executed without immediate human/ground intervention
Rendezvous, proximity operations, docking, berthing or capture events
Degree of simultaneous activities or distributed coordination required
Gap between required capability and demonstrated maturity at program start
Fraction of mission-critical capability without direct flight/surface heritage
Extent to which analogous systems have not operated in comparable environment/regime
Novelty of flight/surface software, autonomy, perception or decision architecture
Thermal range, gradients and cycling imposed on mission-critical hardware
Radiation environment relative to component/system tolerance and mission duration
Degree of regolith contact, plume transport, contamination and abrasive exposure
Variability and duration of illumination interruption affecting thermal/power/ops
Required electrical power and peak-to-average demand relative to architecture
Required absolute/relative localization and control precision
Required delta-v, traverse range, grade, traction or payload mobility performance
Communications availability, latency, data volume/rate and network dependence
Dependence on recurring external consumables, spares or replacement hardware
Dependence on common power, comm, nav, thermal, mobility or servicing assets
Planned maintenance frequency, repair complexity and crew/robotic intervention
Reliance on mobility assets to connect distributed mission functions
Number of organizations with critical design, integration or operational responsibility
Available development time relative to comparable mission complexity/heritage
Novelty and difficulty of verifying integrated surface behavior before flight
Extent/frequency of material requirement changes after architecture baseline
